newsitem.title: UK: Brent, Urals slide, shrugging off Nigeria worry.
newsitem.headline: Brent, Urals slide, shrugging off Nigeria worry.

text.p: Physical Brent blend crude traded lower on Thursday afternoon, leading a downhill slide in values for most grades on a stubbornly oversupplied North Sea wet market, traders said.
Forties cargoes and paper markets also changed hands at weaker numbers, while Ekofisk was done at new lows achieved on Thursday.
Concern about disruption to Shell's Nigerian operations from political disturbances was overshadowed by the slew of first decade Brents available for sale.
"It all looks very, very soft, a trader said.
"Next week will be very bad indeed for Dated," he added.

Communal unrest in Nigeria cut daily crude output by 10 percent this week and threatens to disrupt exports, oil officials said. Shell said exports would be disrupted if the disturbances did not end soon.
A wet Brent loading April 3-5 sold for May Brent -88 cents, eight cents easier than a 2-4 loader sold in the morning. A third Brent was done a quotes-related basis.
Forties loading April 10-12 and 13-15 traded at Dated Brent -15 cents, some five cents weaker. Two further Forties loading around April 12 and April 21 were heard done at similar levels.
Ekofisks loading April 13-15 and April 17-19 changed hands at a three cent discount to Dated, six cents adrift from levels on Tuesday but level with Thursday values.
BP kept all eight cargoes nominated from the paper chains. All eyes were on then fate of five Brents sold by BP on Tuesday and rumoured to be heading either to South Africa or the U.S. Gulf.
A trade of Statfjord was done at the steady level of Dated Brent +7 cents.
Next week's CFD values slipped around 20 cents to May -80/-70 cents.
